narration.text: An annotation can describe a continuous range of text.
But a meaningful unit need not occupy a continuous range.
A single annotation can describe both parts, using a separate segment for each range.

caption: A block contains a sequence of text.

narration.text: Text can also be organised into independent structural containers, called blocks.
What happens if a block is divided inside an annotated range?
The range can become two segments, each belonging to its own block.

caption: Two blocks. Two segments. One annotation.

narration.text: The annotation remains a single object. Its segments have local boundaries, but together they describe one continuous passage.
Merge the blocks again, and adjacent segments can become one.
The annotation survives the structural transformation.

caption: Text has structure. Meaning need not obey it.
